blocks.heading: A mask cannot rescue a routine that is wrong
quotes: “My skin was bad, so I masked every day to speed up recovery.”
“Plump right afterwards, back to normal by morning.”
“A dozen different masks and my skin is no better underneath.”
“I never know whether it goes before or after serum.”

explainer.heading: This is an additional step, and we say so at the top of the page
body: Three steps decide the state of your skin: cleansing properly, moisturising consistently, and daily sun protection. A tube of mask replaces none of them.
The plump feeling straight after is mostly water just delivered into the outermost layer. It is real, but it does not last if the daily moisturising step is still missing.
So when is it worth it? Once the three basics are steady and you want a heavier hydrating step during weeks when skin needs quiet. In that role it does its job well; in any other role it does not.

blocks.heading: Three situations, including one where you should keep your money
blocks.intro: This is the cheapest product in the range, but cheap is not a reason to buy before you need it.

items.heading: Basics are steady, you want a heavier hydrating step
items.body: The role this tube was made for. Once or twice a week, during drier stretches or after a treatment.

items.heading: No sunscreen yet, or moisturising is not consistent
items.body: Spend on those two first. Adding a mask to a routine missing its base is investing in the part that changes least.

items.heading: A lot of active, inflamed breakouts
items.body: A thick gel left sitting on inflamed skin is not a good idea. Deal with the breakout first, then come back to this step.

blocks.heading: Eight ingredients printed on the tube
blocks.intro: The formula belongs to the hydrating and calming group, with nothing acting on pigment.
blocks.caption: This table lists exactly the ingredients PRINTED ON THE 100g TUBE. Full INCI list is printed on the packaging.

rows.name: EGF
rows.role: Epidermal growth factor, used as a conditioning ingredient.

rows.name: Epi-On™
rows.role: Biotech active, aimed at calming the skin.

rows.name: Copper peptide
rows.role: A copper peptide complex, a familiar conditioning ingredient.

rows.name: Exosome cica
rows.role: Centella-derived extract, part of the calming group.

rows.name: Sodium hyaluronate
rows.role: The salt form of hyaluronic acid; holds water in the outer layer.

rows.name: Three nano ceramides (liposome-encapsulated)
rows.role: Ceramides at nano scale, building blocks of the skin barrier.

rows.name: Folic acid (vitamin B9)
rows.role: A B-group vitamin used as a conditioning ingredient.

blocks.eyebrow: Where it sits in the week
blocks.heading: Once or twice a week, in the evening
blocks.intro: An addition to the evening routine, not a replacement for part of it.

steps.label: No masking in the morning
steps.note: A gel layer needs time and undisturbed skin. Mornings usually offer neither.

steps.label: Remove make-up and cleanse
steps.note: Skin must be fully clean, or the gel seals in the residue too.

steps.label: Apply a thick layer
steps.note: Avoid the eye and lip areas.

steps.label: Leave it, then rinse with cool water
steps.note: For the time stated on the tube. Longer does not give a better result.

steps.label: Moisturise as usual
steps.note: The mask does not replace the cream step.

blocks.footnote: More than twice a week shortens nothing. Skin renews on its own cycle, and the number of masks does not speed that cycle up.

blocks.heading: Three steps, 15–20 minutes each time
blocks.intro: The amount and timing are taken verbatim from the manufacturer's instructions.

items.heading: Cleanse
items.body: Wash and dry your face before applying.

items.heading: Apply a thin layer
items.body: About 5–10g, roughly three fingertip joints, for one use.

items.heading: Leave 15–20 minutes, then rinse
items.body: Rinse with clean water, then moisturise as usual.

blocks.footnote: This is an optional step, not a required one. If this week you only manage the three basics — cleanse, moisturise, sun protection — skipping the mask makes no difference to the routine's outcome.

blocks.heading: If you can only pick one for a recovery phase
blocks.intro: The honest answer: buy the moisturiser first. Here is why.

items.q: How often should I use it?
items.a: The manufacturer does not publish a frequency, so we do not quote one. For a hydrating and calming formula, how often you mask matters far less than whether the three basics happen consistently.
Yes. The manufacturer states leaving it 15–20 minutes and then rinsing with clean water, followed by a moisturiser.

items.q: Can I use it during a pigmentation routine?
items.a: Yes, because it is a hydrating step with nothing acting on pigment, so it does not compete with the cream or serum. But if your skin is stinging, the answer is to remove steps rather than add one.
Somewhere dry and cool, away from direct sunlight and heat. Close the cap after use.

blocks.heading: The three base steps that come first
blocks.intro: If any of these three is missing, that is where the money goes before a mask.
